competitors.name: Meetup.com
competitors.description: Platform for finding and building local communities around shared interests.
complaints: Expensive organizer fees ($30+/mo) drive community leaders away
Search algorithm pushes paid sponsored events over organic grassroots clubs
High ghosting/no-show rate on RSVP'd events with zero accountability
Interface is cluttered with promoted content, killing the organic discovery vibe

competitors.name: Discord
competitors.description: Voice, video, and text communication service used by millions of groups.
complaints: Overwhelming notifications and unorganized chat channels
Not optimized for in-person real-world event coordination and attendance commitments
Moderation tools are crude and communities devolve into toxicity quickly

competitors.name: Eventbrite
competitors.description: Ticketing and event management platform for organizers of all sizes.
complaints: Takes massive platform fees on top of payment processing fees
Designed for large commercial events, not casual 5-person hobby hangouts
No social features — you attend an event and never connect with attendees again

competitors.name: Bumble BFF
competitors.description: Friend-finding mode within the Bumble dating app ecosystem.
complaints: Swipe fatigue — treating friendship like dating feels shallow and transactional
No shared activity or interest matching, just photos and bios
People match and then never actually meet in person — zero follow-through mechanics

raw_complaint_pool: I just want to find 3 people to play board games with nearby without paying a $30 monthly subscription.
People RSVP to events and then 80% ghost without penalty.
Finding genuine in-person friends after college feels impossible on existing ad-filled feeds.
Every 'social' app is actually designed to keep you scrolling, not to get you out of the house.
I moved to a new city and it took 8 months to find a single friend group. Apps made it harder, not easier.
Meetup charges organizers $200/year to run a free hiking group that benefits the community. It's predatory.
I've been on Bumble BFF for a year. Matched with 40 people. Met exactly zero in person.
The loneliness epidemic is real and tech companies are profiting from it instead of solving it.
